sources.citation: J. Zihl, D. Von Cramon, N. Mai (1983). SELECTIVE DISTURBANCE OF MOVEMENT VISION AFTER BILATERAL BRAIN DAMAGE. Brain.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1983) in Brain establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: J. Zihl, D. Von Cramon, N. Mai, CH. Schmid (1991). DISTURBANCE OF MOVEMENT VISION AFTER BILATERAL POSTERIOR BRAIN DAMAGE: FURTHER EVIDENCE AND FOLLOW UP OBSERVATIONS. Brain.
sources.notes: Zihl, von Cramon, Mai & Schmid (1991 Brain) longitudinal follow-up on Patient L.M. confirming persistent multi-target visual motion deficits a decade post-lesion.

sources.citation: S. Zeki (1991). CEREBRAL AKINETOPSIA (VISUAL MOTION BLINDNESS). Brain.
sources.notes: Zeki (1991 Brain) foundational synthesis of cerebral akinetopsia and functional specialization of human visual motion area V5/MT.

sources.citation: Matthew Rizzo, Mark Nawrot, Josef Zihl (1995). Motion and shape perception in cerebral akinetopsia. Brain.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1995) in Brain extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Johanna L. Browne, Lydia Krabbendam, Jan Dirk Blom (2025). Akinetopsia: a systematic review on visual motion blindness. Frontiers in Neurology.
sources.notes: Johanna L. Browne (2025) peer-reviewed review in Frontiers in Neurology: Akinetopsia: a systematic review on visual motion blindness.

sources.citation: Lucas Henriques Viscardi, Fabricio Diniz Kleber, Henrique Custódio, Angelo Brandelli Costa et al. (2024). Akinetopsia (visual motion blindness) associated with brain metastases: a case report. Neurological Sciences.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2024) in Neurological Sciences extending the foundational findings.
